This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.77% of all local loads and 53.21% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 13.55% of all sectors requested in L2.

This workload accesses local memory (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses), accounting for 38.28% of all sectors requested in L1TEX. Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.90% of all local loads and 48.49% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.45% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.79% of all local loads and 48.39% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.39% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.84% of all local loads and 47.55% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.19% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.92% of all local loads and 47.95% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.31% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). This workload accesses local memory (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses), accounting for 38.28% of all sectors requested in L1TEX. Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.79% of all local loads and 48.31% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.38% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). For more advice on how to reduce the usage of local memory refer to the documentation (https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#metrics-hw-memory)."

Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.86% of all local loads and 48.14% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.34% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.78% of all local loads and 48.12% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.32% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.74% of all local loads and 48.30% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.36% of all sectors requested in L2.
One common reason for the use of local memory is arrays being too large to fit into registers or not being indexed using compile time constants (see the Local Memory" section of the CUDA Programming Guide (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#device-memory-accesses). Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 2.03% of all local loads and 47.61% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.25% of all sectors requested in L2.

This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.79% of all local loads and 48.32% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.37% of all sectors requested in L2.

Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.84% of all local loads and 47.48% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.18% of all sectors requested in L2.

Local memory refers to a memory space that is private to each thread. Although it is logically distinct, local memory resides in global memory. This can lead to higher memory latency compared to the usage of registers or shared memory, a decrease in available bandwidth to global memory, and an increase in executed instructions.
All of the local memory accesses are due to register spilling (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html#variable-memory-space-specifiers). 1.80% of all local loads and 47.90% of all local stores spill into the L2 cache, accounting for 12.28% of all sectors requested in L2.
